growth_signal.value: Raised a $48M Series A led by Accel, and its own site claims it supports 2.6 million properties worldwide, with new partnerships announced with Grab and Attijariwafa bank in 2026.

entry.idea: Building a hotel-booking or travel product usually means wrestling with hundreds of different hotel and pricing systems, so Nuitée sells ready-made APIs that plug any company straight into hotel rates, availability and bookings worldwide.
entry.lesson: Instead of competing for customers in a crowded market, sell the infrastructure that lets many other companies enter that market easily.
entry.name: Nuitée

growth.basis: substitute: new partnerships (Grab, Attijariwafa bank) and headcount growth
growth.reason: It has grown to 300+ employees and landed a $48M round and new partnerships with Grab and a major bank, but no revenue or booking-volume numbers are public.

market.reason: Hotel and travel distribution is a large global industry, and Nuitée's own materials cite the B2B hotel market at $75 billion.

tech.reason: API infrastructure for hotel distribution is solid engineering, but similar aggregation and connectivity platforms already exist in travel tech, so it is not hard for a strong team to approach.

entry.twist: It calls itself the 'Stripe for travel': other companies, from banks to super-apps like Grab, use Nuitée's building blocks to add hotel booking into their own products without building travel infrastructure themselves.
entry.who_pays: Travel companies, banks, super-apps and other businesses pay to use Nuitée's APIs to power hotel search, pricing and booking inside their own products.
entry.why_now: AI-driven travel booking and agentic apps are growing fast, and companies outside travel (banks, ride-hailing apps) increasingly want to bolt on booking features quickly rather than build them from scratch.
